The benchmark:\\n\\n* Is applicable to Amazon EC2 nodes (both managed and self-managed) where you are responsible for security configurations of Kubernetes components.\\n* Provides a standard, community-approved way to ensure that you have configured your Kubernetes cluster and nodes securely when using Amazon EKS.\\n* Consists of four sections; control plane logging configuration, node security configurations, policies, and managed services.\\n* Supports all of the Kubernetes versions currently available in Amazon EKS and can be run using kube-bench, a standard open source tool for checking configuration using the CIS benchmark on Kubernetes clusters.\\n\\nTo learn more, see Introducing The CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark.\\n\\nFor an automated `aws-sample` pipeline to update your node group with a CIS benchmarked AMI, see EKS-Optimized AMI Hardening Pipeline\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/configuration-vulnerability-analysis.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Protecting the infrastructure (hosts)\",\"context\":\"### Periodically run kube-bench to verify compliance with CIS benchmarks for Kubernetes\\n\\nkube-bench is an open source project from Aqua that evaluates your\\ncluster against the CIS benchmarks for Kubernetes. The benchmark\\ndescribes the best practices for securing unmanaged Kubernetes clusters.\\nThe CIS Kubernetes Benchmark encompasses the control plane and the data\\nplane. Since Amazon EKS provides a fully managed control plane, not all\\nof the recommendations from the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark are applicable.\\nTo ensure this scope reflects how Amazon EKS is implemented, AWS created\\nthe *CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark*. The EKS benchmark inherits from CIS\\nKubernetes Benchmark with additional inputs from the community with\\nspecific configuration considerations for EKS clusters.\\n\\nWhen running kube-bench\\nagainst an EKS cluster, follow\\nthese\\ninstructions from Aqua Security. For further information see\\nIntroducing\\nThe CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/protecting-the-infrastructure.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"CIS AWS Benchmark v1.4.0\",\"context\":\"## What is the CIS AWS Benchmark?\\n\\nThe CIS AWS Benchmark v1.4.0 provides prescriptive guidance for configuring security\\noptions for a subset of Amazon Web Services. It has an emphasis on foundational, testable, and\\narchitecture agnostic settings. Some of the specific Amazon Web Services in scope for this document\\ninclude the following:\\n\\n* AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)\\n* IAM Access Analyzer\\n* AWS Config\\n* AWS CloudTrail\\n* Amazon CloudWatch\\n* Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)\\n* Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)\\n* Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)\\n* Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)\\n* Amazon Virtual Private Cloud\\n\\n###### Difference between CIS Benchmarks and CIS Controls\\n\\nThe *CIS Benchmarks* are security best practice\\nguidelines that are specific to vendor products. Ranging from operating systems to cloud\\nservices and networks devices, the settings that are applied from a benchmark protect\\nthe systems that are being used. The *CIS Controls* are\\nfoundational best practice guidelines for your organization to follow to help protect\\nfrom known cyberattack vectors.\\n\\n###### Examples\\n\\n* CIS Benchmarks are prescriptive. They typically reference a specific setting that\\n can be reviewed and set in the vendor product.\\n\\n **Example:** CIS AWS Benchmark v1.3.0 - Ensure MFA\\n is enabled for the \\\"root user\\\" account\\n\\n This recommendation provides prescriptive guidance on how to check for this and\\n how to set this on the root account for the AWS environment.\\n* CIS Controls are for your organization as a whole, and aren't specific to only one\\n vendor product.\\n\\n **Example:** CIS v7.1 - Use Multi-Factor\\n Authentication for All Administrative Access\\n\\n This control describes what's expected to be applied within your organization.\\n However, it doesn't describe how to apply it for the systems and workloads that you're\\n running, regardless of where they are\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/audit-manager/latest/userguide/CIS-1-4.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up CIS EKS Benchmark v1.8.0 controls", "parent_id": "47e62248-33ba-4f88-831a-e3d14c8bfb3c"}

Since Amazon EKS provides a fully managed control plane, not all\\nof the recommendations from the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark are applicable.\\nTo ensure this scope reflects how Amazon EKS is implemented, AWS created\\nthe *CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark*. The benchmark:\\n\\n* Is applicable to Amazon EC2 nodes (both managed and self-managed) where you are responsible for security configurations of Kubernetes components.\\n* Provides a standard, community-approved way to ensure that you have configured your Kubernetes cluster and nodes securely when using Amazon EKS.\\n* Consists of four sections; control plane logging configuration, node security configurations, policies, and managed services.\\n* Supports all of the Kubernetes versions currently available in Amazon EKS and can be run using kube-bench, a standard open source tool for checking configuration using the CIS benchmark on Kubernetes clusters.\\n\\nTo learn more, see Introducing The CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark.\\n\\nFor an automated `aws-sample` pipeline to update your node group with a CIS benchmarked AMI, see EKS-Optimized AMI Hardening Pipeline\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/configuration-vulnerability-analysis.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Harden Kubernetes RBAC in Amazon EKS\",\"context\":\"## Recommended controls\\n\\n### Scope RBAC to least privilege\\n\\n* Review the ClusterRoles bound to CSI driver and DaemonSet service accounts. Remove permissions that are not required for your workloads.\\n* For the EBS CSI driver, set `node.serviceAccount.disableMutation` to `true` if you don\u2019t use the taint removal feature.\\n* Use `kubectl auth can-i --list --as=system:serviceaccount:NAMESPACE:SERVICE_ACCOUNT` to audit effective permissions.\\n\\n### Enforce Pod security standards\\n\\nApply the Kubernetes Pod Security Standards using the built-in Pod Security Admission controller or a policy engine. At minimum, enforce the `baseline` profile cluster-wide and the `restricted` profile for workload namespaces. This limits the ability to create privileged containers outside of system namespaces.\\n\\n### Use network policies\\n\\nApply network policies to restrict egress from CSI driver and DaemonSet Pods to only the endpoints they need (for example, the Kubernetes API server and AWS service endpoints). This reduces the scope of actions possible.\\n\\n### Monitor RBAC activity\\n\\nEnable Kubernetes audit logging and monitor for unexpected API calls from DaemonSet service accounts. Look for:\\n\\n* Node modifications from CSI driver service accounts\\n* Pod creation in system namespaces\\n* Unusual `get` or `list` calls on Secrets\\n\\nFor more information, see Send control plane logs to CloudWatch Logs\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/rbac-hardening.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"aws-iam\",\"skill_description\":\"Provides verified corrections for IAM behaviors that AI agents frequently get wrong \u2014 policy evaluation edge cases, trust policy gotchas, STS session limits, Organizations quirks, and SAML/MFA specifics. Also provides structured workflows for IAM role management and baseline policy generation from application source code or a Terraform plan JSON. Covers condition operator safety (ForAnyValue/ForAllValues with Null checks), bucket policy deny patterns (VPC endpoint restrictions, org paths), confused deputy protection, and service role creation for AWS services (Glue, CloudTrail, Lambda, ECS, etc.) with aws:SourceAccount/aws:SourceArn trust conditions. Applies when creating IAM roles, writing IAM or bucket policies, generating policies from application source code or a Terraform plan JSON, working with STS, Organizations, or condition operators, or any task needing a service or execution role. Does not cover non-IAM authorization like Cognito user-pool policies or app-level RBAC.\\n\\n\\nServices: iam, sts, organizations\\nTasks: deploy, configure, secure, policy-generation, permissions, source-code-to-policy, terraform-plan-to-policy\\nPersona: developer, devops, architect, security-engineer\\nWorkload: serverless, containers, data-analytics, security\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"aws-iam\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search docs for CIS EKS Benchmark section 4 titles", "parent_id": "04e02365-309d-4acb-bdd1-6cc2f5cad1f1"}
